source_of_truth: Derived by hand from the build I wrote, not from the tool: the /app route's client-reference manifest lists static/chunks/heavy-vendor.js in clientModules with async:false, so it is part of the route's INITIAL client set (not a lazy chunk). That chunk is 300000 bytes raw of high-entropy base64; gzip on disk is 227272 bytes = 221.9 KB, far above route-attribution's 150 KB heuristic for a single initial chunk. A route shipping a ~222 KB gzip chunk on first load is a genuine initial-weight defect worth confirming. route-heavy-initial-chunk is HEURISTIC by design (hashed chunk names hide the library), so heuristic is the strongest honest level.

expected.rationale: heavy-vendor.js (221.9 KB gzip) sits in /app's initial client set (async:false in the client-reference manifest) and is the largest initial chunk, over the 150 KB threshold; this is the defect-level signal this auditor emits for bundle weight. line is null because the finding is attributed to a route PATH, not a source line.
